site: ADP recruitment posting; shared browser submission guard
class: An action label shared by opening and final submission was classified without DOM context
symptom: A live application paused on the job posting, before any application fields appeared, because clicking Apply was intercepted as final submission.
root_cause: The browser guard treated every Apply label as final, although Python considered the page a posting. Posting detection also rejected any submit-type button even without an associated form. The PageAgent opening exception depended on the planner's page_kind instead of independent DOM evidence.
fix: Share a conservative posting-Apply DOM predicate between the browser firewall, posting detection, and PageAgent. Require job-description evidence and absence of application/review state; preserve final submission containment and remember application DOM state within the guarded document. Ignore only hidden recognized OneTrust cookie utility controls; hidden applicant state remains blocking.
prevention: Validate the actual DOM independently of planner classifications and test an opening Apply transitioning into a guarded final Apply in the same document. Never disable submission protection to open the form.
why_tests_missed: Existing containment tests covered final Apply labels but never a posting Apply transitioning into the application, or a posting with hidden cookie utilities. The first new synthetic posting also omitted those real cookie controls.
